anomalies.obs: R3 is drawn as 10 (ohms) between the +5V rail and the RST global label (which feeds MCU pin 1, J1.4 and J4.5). It is the only element holding the reset line high, i.e. the reset pull-up.
anomalies.expected: A reset pull-up should be in the 10 kΩ range, consistent with the other pull-ups on this sheet (R1 = 10K gate pull-up, R6 = 10K TACH pull-up). A 10 Ω pull-up is three orders of magnitude too low.

evidence.quote: R3 10 between +5V and RST (sheet /, page 1, top centre)
R1 10K and R6 10K used as pull-ups elsewhere on the same sheet

anomalies.impact: The reset line is stiffly tied to +5V through 10 Ω; any device that pulls RESET low (e.g. the ISP programmer on J4, or a transient) forces ~0.5 A through R3, and the intended high-impedance pull-up behaviour is lost. This is a deviation from the reference pull-up value.

anomalies.obs: On the right tile, U1 (LM1117-5.0) pin 3 (VI, input) and pin 2 (VO, output) are both wired to the +5V arrow; the VCC net (the raw supply from J5, decoupled by C1) does not reach the regulator input.
anomalies.expected: The LM1117-5.0 input (VI) must be connected to the unregulated VCC supply so it can generate the +5V rail; tying VI to VO bypasses the regulator and leaves +5V without a source.

evidence.quote: U1 LM1117-5.0, pin 3 VI and pin 2 VO both to +5V (sheet /, right tile, top)
VCC net appears only at J5.2, C1 and JP1.2, not at U1.VI

anomalies.impact: If this reading is correct, the +5V rail is never powered from VCC and the MCU (whose pin 8 is tied to +5V) would not start. Lower confidence because the input arrow label is hard to disambiguate from VCC at this resolution.

parsed.summary: The drawing supports at least one deviation: the reset pull-up R3 is 10 Ω instead of the ~10 kΩ used for every other pull-up on the sheet (R1, R6), which is three orders of magnitude off; a possible second issue is the LM1117 input pin tied to +5V rather than VCC, though that reading is less certain.
